schemaVersion: 1

name: structured-concurrency
version: 1.3.5
description: >-
  StructuredTaskScope as a lifetime guarantee for a fan-out: fork, join, close, and the rule
  that no subtask thread outlives the block. Covers the API as it stands on each JDK — still
  a preview API on every released version, renamed between 25 and 26 and changed again in
  27 — the Joiner completion policies, scope timeouts, nesting, and what close actually
  waits for. Use when writing or reviewing a parallel fan-out inside one request, when a
  sibling task keeps running after another failed, when code copied from a blog uses
  ShutdownOnFailure or a StructuredTaskScope constructor, when preview class files fail to
  run on a different JDK, when a scope fails in milliseconds and closes in seconds, or when
  Subtask.get is called before join. Not why cancellation fails to arrive
  (cancellation-and-interruption), context inherited by subtasks (scoped-values), the
  threads underneath (thread-sizing-and-virtual-threads), or callback graphs
  (completablefuture-composition).

findings.priorProblem: The Stop at a condition row declared allUntil unchanged in JDK 26 and 27.
findings.evidence: Official JDK 25 Joiner returns Stream<Subtask<T>>; JDK 26 and 27 Joiner return List<Subtask<T>>. JDK 25 allUntil join throws on timeout; JDK 26 onTimeout for allUntil does not throw and JDK 27 allUntil also returns the subtask list on timeout.
findings.consequence: Copying the table can produce non-compiling collection use and a timeout fallback/metric that silently stops running after migration.
findings.correction: Corrected result and timeout rows; routed consumers from SKILL.md and the JDK 25 example reference to the version matrix.

findings.priorProblem: The version guidance did not connect normal allUntil return after timeout to per-subtask state handling and timeout observation.
findings.evidence: JDK 26/27 allUntil documentation explicitly permits returned UNAVAILABLE subtasks after timeout; predicate-driven early cancellation can also yield unavailable work.
findings.consequence: Normal join return could be misread as all-success, get could be called on an unavailable result, and timeout could be confused with another cancellation cause.
findings.correction: Require state inspection and a version-correct timeout observation contract; explain why a catch-only timeout metric or fallback copied from JDK 25 misses the built-in JDK 26/27 timeout path.

findings.priorProblem: The examples' migration routing framed JDK 26 changes mainly as Joiner names, while custom callback parameter types also drift.
findings.evidence: JDK 25 onFork/onComplete use Subtask<? extends T>; JDK 26/27 use Subtask<T>. Predicate types must also be read from the target API.
findings.consequence: A JDK 25 custom override pasted into a later preview can fail to override/compile.
findings.correction: Documented the callback difference and widened the existing routing sentence to signatures and timeout behavior, leaving example targets intact.
